# Calibration results

*Ported* = core as ported from the prior engine (sloped-hopper build-up, Cb 0.85). *Calibrated* = hold-type k × L·B·D and the fitted Cb, from `factors.yaml`.

## Fitted factors

- **k, box hold:** 0.1086 t/m³ (range 0.095–0.1223, n = 2)
- **k, container hold:** 0.1711 t/m³ (range 0.1711–0.1711, n = 1)
- **Cb, box barge on LOA:** 0.927 (range 0.882–0.994, n = 7; 2 excluded — see factors.yaml)

## Calibration Bands

Each observed figure has a band, set per figure and per confidence of the case (`bands.yaml`): lightship ±15 / 20 / 30 % and deadweight ±7.5 / 10 / 15 % at high / medium / low confidence. The band applies to the *Calibrated* result. **The errors in sections 1 and 2 are in-sample:** the fitted factors (k per hold type, box-barge Cb) were fitted to the same cases, and the container factor rests on one case, so a result inside its band is not a validation. **The errors in section 4 are out of sample:** those cases were never used in a fit. A case outside its band is marked **OUTSIDE** and raises a CI warning annotation: **warning only, it never fails the build.** A lightship given only as an upper bound has no band. Section 3 compares the core with a design note, not a published figure, and has no band.

12 of 13 in-sample calibrated results are inside their band.
67 of 87 held-out calibrated results are inside their band (section 4; cases excluded for an impossible figure are not counted).

## 4. Held-out cases (out of sample)

These cases were never used to fit k or Cb (issue #3). The calibrated model meets each one for the first time here, so these errors are out of sample. A deck barge has hold type `deck` and is run as a box barge (`run_as: box`): box k and box Cb, with no deck factor. The test is whether the box model carries over to deck barges. Predicted DWT uses the water density on the case: 1.025 for sea-going or saltwater figures, 1.000 otherwise. Cargo capacity is not DWT, so it is shown against the predicted DWT but has no band. ## 5. Type C tank cases (held out)

One cargo tank, run through the tank maths only (`tank_cases.yaml`, bands in `tank_bands.yaml`). Every case is held out: it is never used to fit a factor. The engine's tank diameter is the outside of the insulation, so each source's diameter and length are first brought to that datum (`diameter_basis`, `length_basis`). Volume and steel are run at the published shell thickness; the wall is the pressure-vessel formula at the steel diameter, with the material the case says it is run as. **Steel weight of the first case is in-sample for the structure factor** of fully pressurised LPG in the Defaults Profile, which was worked out from that one published weight. A miss is a warning only.

### Tank weight per m³ (published records, issue #317)

Published empty weights of marine LNG Type C tanks over their gross volume. They are the check on the tank structure factor before it is tuned. A record runs only when its diameter and length have a stated basis; none has one yet, so none is run.

## 5a. Tank barges (issue #335)

Every `hold_type: tank` record of `cases.yaml` and the reference vessels of `tank_barge_cases.yaml`, run through the tank-barge model: lightship = k × L·B·D + outfit (k = 0.1141 t/m³, an Estimate; outfit coefficients are Estimates), and the deadweight at the stated draught is the box-barge Cb × L·B·T·ρ less that lightship. Bands are in `tank_barge_bands.yaml`: starting values for the maintainer, equal to the dry-barge bands. **The 15 cases of the k-fit subset are in-sample** (k was fitted on them, from the same deadweights); every other case is out of sample. A **self-propelled** vessel has no band: the model has no machinery, accommodation or fuel, so its deadweight comes out too high by about that weight. A cargo capacity is not a deadweight, so it is shown against the predicted deadweight and has no band. A band miss is a warning only.

## 6. Bollard pull (propulsion cases, spec 0007)

Tugs and pushers with a published bollard pull, run through the Propulsor model only (`propulsion_cases.yaml`, band `bollard_pull_t` in `bands.yaml`): kappa_b x (2 rho A)^(1/3) P_D^(2/3) per unit, P_D the published power through the spec 0007 transmission (gearbox 0.97 for engine power; shaft line 0.99, azimuth drive 0.95). The in-sample cases of a type fit its kappa_b; **their errors are in-sample**. Held-out cases were never used in the fit. A miss is a warning only.

### Fitted bollard pull factors

- **azimuth_open:** kappa_b 0.77 (no in-sample case: the open-propeller value (Wartsila, k2 = 1), an estimate)
- **azimuth_ducted:** kappa_b 0.975 (range 0.917–1.063, n = 3)
- **shaft_open:** kappa_b 0.77 (no in-sample case: the open-propeller value (Wartsila, k2 = 1), an estimate)
- **shaft_nozzle:** kappa_b 0.951 (range 0.939–0.963, n = 2)
- **voith_schneider:** kappa_b 0.77 (no in-sample case: the open-propeller value (Wartsila, k2 = 1), an estimate)
- **pump_jet:** kappa_b 0.77 (no in-sample case: the open-propeller value (Wartsila, k2 = 1), an estimate)

## 7. Installed power (spec 0007)

Inland ships that print both the installed power and a design speed, run through the whole engine: the hull at its printed size and maximum draught, its propulsors, and the Installed Power sized for the design speed in deep water with the 1.20 margin. The in-sample cases of a type fit its efficiency factor kappa; **their errors are in-sample**. A miss is a warning only.

### Fitted efficiency factors

- **azimuth_open:** kappa 0.8 (no in-sample case: the starting estimate)
- **azimuth_ducted:** kappa 0.8 (no in-sample case: the starting estimate)
- **shaft_open:** kappa 0.8 (no in-sample case: the starting estimate)
- **shaft_nozzle:** kappa 0.437 (n = 1)
- **voith_schneider:** kappa 0.8 (no in-sample case: the starting estimate)
- **pump_jet:** kappa 0.8 (no in-sample case: the starting estimate)
